messages:
Alyssa: heads-up, saw a p95 latency regression on prod after enabling structured-output + toolcall opt-in. traces show lots of parked requests holding queue slots. anyone else?
Sam: yup, spotted it this morning during canary. profiler shows tool pauses are fragmenting batch shapes — leads to kernel hops + KV churn.
Jordan: quick numbers from last night: before change p95=180ms p99=340ms; after enabling structured-output+fncall p95=420ms p99=1.1s. throughput roughly flat. kernel_swap_count per req +2.3x.
Mike: dropping one example trace we captured on staging:
```text
trace_id=abc123 stage=decode batch_id=987 epoch=12 kernel=gegl16 -> kern=gevq32 swap_ts=1612ms kv_epoch=5 kv_miss=1 parked=true pause_ms=450
trace_id=abc124 stage=decode batch_id=988 kernel=gevq32 -> kern=gegl16 swap_ts=1703ms kv_epoch=5 kv_miss=0 parked=false
```
Alyssa: interesting — hypothesis: when a request enters a toolcall/structured-output park we retain the batch slot and keep the kernel pinned. kernel_hysteresis is too small so the router swaps to a smaller kernel for other work and then swaps back when the original resumes -> thrash.
Sam: also seeing KV eviction on resume. parked requests with long pauses let older KV pages age out; refill on resume is expensive. so resume cost = kernel_swap + kv_refill.
Jordan: ran quick staging experiments: increasing batch_park_timeout from 50ms -> 200ms cut kernel swaps by ~45% and brought p95 down to ~260ms (p50 rose slightly).
Mike: config snippet we used in the experiment: 
```json
{
  "batch_park_timeout_ms": "200",
  "parked_token_budget": "16",
  "kernel_hysteresis_ms": "80",
  "prefetch_kv_on_toolcall": "true"
}
```
Alyssa: what does prefetch_kv_on_toolcall do exactly?
Sam: when we detect a toolcall pause we snapshot the last N KV pages and asynchronously pin/prefetch them into GPU memory if we predict a fast resume (based on parked_token_budget and route history). avoids the refill hit.
Jordan: caveat: extra memory pressure. rule-of-thumb: only prefetch if seq_len > 512 or resume_confidence > 0.6. otherwise skip.
Mike: we also experimented with a stop_token_probe: a lightweight early scan for structured-output boundaries to short-circuit parks. the probe runs a tiny fp16 kernel on the last 8 tokens. it reduced parked_count by ~18% in staging.
Alyssa: nice — so two levers: avoid unnecessary parking via stop_probe, and mitigate resume cost via prefetch + higher park timeout + hysteresis.
Sam: code branch stop_probe_v2 in runtime/park_hints has the probe + telemetry. also added telemetry: parked_count, avg_park_ms, kernel_swap_count, kv_miss_on_resume.
Jordan: proposed rollout plan: 1) land kernel_hysteresis + batch_park_timeout behind a runtime flag and canary; 2) prototype prefetch_kv_on_toolcall as tenant opt-in; 3) enable stop_token_probe in staging only. metrics to watch: kernel_swap_count, parked_count, kv_miss_per_resume, p95/p99 latency.
Alyssa: owners: Sam -> flag rollout + instrumentation, Mike -> prefetch prototype + memory safety checks, Jordan -> dashboards/alerts for the new metrics. I'll open a PR with default values and write up the canary checklist.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: canary=park-hints-flag at 2026-03-19T22:00:00Z (22:00 UTC).
Mike: will post staging numbers tomorrow after a few hours of load. :thumbsup:
Alyssa: thanks team — let's keep the changes behind flags until we validate KV memory and tail latency.
